tasks.short: Maintain appointment and event calendars, resolve clashes, and confirm arrangements.

steps.what: Read appointment requests and establish participants, duration, location, and constraints.

loop.input: Appointment request and permitted scheduling defaults.
loop.output: Proposed participants, duration, location, dates, and constraints.
loop.check: Validate identities, dates, and required fields; show supporting request text.
loop.stop: One extraction per request; incomplete or contradictory requests enter the assistant's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms handle structured requests; remaining requests contain free-text constraints.

steps.what: Check participant availability, room capacity, and existing commitments.
Negotiate alternatives when requested times or resources conflict.
Decide whether priority exceptions justify moving existing commitments.
Create or update calendar entries and reserve rooms.
Send confirmations and explain changed arrangements to participants.

tasks.design: Configure booking rules, room resources, and availability checks in the {CALENDAR}; use a {WORKFLOW} form for standard requests. A bounded extraction step prepares requests arriving through {EMAIL}, while the assistant negotiates clashes and the organiser approves priority exceptions. Approved arrangements update the {CALENDAR} and generate confirmations for recipient checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking features already exist, but delegated calendar rights, room rules, and requests scattered across mailboxes limit their use.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking configuration handles most mechanics. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting request intake and exception queues.
tasks.still_hard: External availability, late changes, competing priorities, and incomplete room information still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands which inconvenience participants will accept and handles sensitive changes tactfully.

ambition.what: Weekly adjustment of bookable room capacity using aggregate demand.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving contested arrangements and proposing room-capacity changes. With explicit delegation, the assistant can adjust routine booking windows; priority decisions remain with organisers.

reach.task: Review recurring room shortages and propose capacity adjustments.
reach.learn: Room-capacity planning, accessibility requirements, and aggregate utilisation analysis.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn a mail thread into a meeting invitation with an agenda.
The department trial found scheduling took longer on average; model-based scheduling gains are not assured.
Availability checks, resource booking, and reminders can usually use existing configuration.

assumptions: Shared calendars and bookable room resources are typical; a spreadsheet is not the primary diary.
Routine bookings follow standing delegation; the organiser decision step covers exceptions only.
Time shares average routine bookings and cases requiring negotiation.
Internal calendar writes and external invitations can be controlled separately.
Build ranges cover one department and existing calendar interfaces.
GDPR requires appropriate calendar access and data minimisation. National rules may require employee consultation for usage reporting.
unknowns: Calendar delegation, room-resource quality, and available interfaces.
Which bookings may proceed under standing delegation.
Whether internal calendar updates automatically notify external participants.
Applicable national consultation requirements and consultation lead time.
research_questions: Does configured booking remove more handling time than free-text intake assistance?
How often do conflicts require organiser judgment rather than another available slot?
new_work: Review extracted constraints and unresolved identities.
Maintain booking windows, room rules, and delegated permissions.
Handle failed updates and duplicate requests.
Review aggregate room demand without tracking individual performance.

tasks.short: Prepare meeting notes, routine correspondence, and recurring reports, then obtain approval and distribute them.

steps.what: Collect source records and figures for correspondence and recurring reports.
Attend meetings and record decisions, discussion points, and actions.

loop.output: Draft notes with decisions, action owners, deadlines, and transcript references.
loop.check: Check decisions against transcript references; mark disputed statements and missing owners.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unclear passages return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken discussion does not follow a fixed field structure.

steps.what: Draft routine correspondence and turn meeting notes into readable minutes.

loop.input: Source pack or reviewed meeting notes, approved template, and intended audience.
loop.output: Correspondence or minutes draft with source references.
loop.check: Require support for factual claims; compare names, dates, commitments, and actions with sources.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported content is removed or escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed wording uses templates; variable narrative still requires language drafting.

steps.what: Compile tables, charts, and presentation pages for recurring reports.
Check accuracy, resolve disputed wording, and approve the document and recipients.
Distribute approved documents and record the released version.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration gathers approved records from the {ERP}, {EXPENSE}, and {DOCS}, then fills report templates deterministically. Bounded drafting steps prepare minutes and variable correspondence in the {DOCS}, with source references and unresolved questions. A {WORKFLOW} approval binds the final version and recipient list before distribution through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources, templates, and approval trails are fragmented. Variable narrative is harder to template than tables and standard letters.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration and template development make recurring outputs cheaper to build. Bounded language drafting can prepare narrative for review.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous decisions, disputed wording, poor source data, and sensitive recipients require careful review. Recording meetings also introduces access, retention, and consultation work.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant distinguishes a tentative comment from an agreed decision and writes for the audience's actual needs.

ambition.what: A plain-language monthly operations briefing for staff without desk-based roles.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from typing and formatting toward checking evidence and helping document owners explain decisions. The assistant can propose audience-specific briefings; publication authority stays with document owners.

reach.task: Maintain an agreed action register from approved meeting decisions.
reach.learn: Action ownership, dependencies, deadline tracking, and escalation practice.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Teams Facilitator supports live meeting notes.
The department evaluation reported drafting and meeting-summary time savings, but no evidence of higher productivity and some hallucinations.
The Netherlands' works-council rules cited in the digest cover relevant recording and monitoring arrangements.
Routine drafting and minutes are not themselves listed in Annex III; staff monitoring or task allocation changes the assessment.

assumptions: The task combines alternative document routes; each document does not pass through both meeting capture and report compilation.
Time shares represent the combined document workload, including document-owner review.
Numerical reports use approved definitions and deterministic calculations.
Distribution sends only the exact approved version to the approved recipients; changes invalidate approval.
Build ranges cover a few recurring templates and one meeting environment.
GDPR applies to meeting capture and document handling. Recording requires a lawful basis, defined access, retention, and a DPIA where required.
National rules determine employee consultation; the Dutch rule in the digest does not apply automatically elsewhere. Formal consultation may exceed the estimated working days.
unknowns: The workload split between reports, correspondence, and minutes.
Which meetings may be recorded and whether transcripts already exist.
Document owners, recipient approval rules, and publication permissions.
research_questions: Which documents can use templates without model drafting?
Does source-linked review reduce total preparation and correction time?
What recording and retention configuration satisfies the intended meeting use?
new_work: Check narrative claims and disputed meeting decisions.
Maintain templates, report definitions, and source mappings.
Handle failed distributions and approval invalidation.
Train users to review generated drafts and recognise unsupported statements.

tasks.short: Complete administrative forms from source records, obtain required approval, and submit them.

steps.what: Identify the correct form, current version, and procedural requirements.
Retrieve required employee or financial details from authorised records.
Enter details, calculate required values, and check mandatory fields.
Resolve exceptions and approve forms requiring authorisation.
Submit the approved form through the internal request process.
Save a separate copy and update the local submission log.

tasks.design: A configured request in the {WORKFLOW} selects the current form and retrieves permitted fields from the {HCM} or {ERP}. Deterministic mappings generate the form, validate it, and route exceptions or required approvals to the process owner. The {WORKFLOW} retains the approved version and submission record, removing duplicate local filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms were designed as documents, with inconsistent field names and manual copying between records and submission processes.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes field mappings, validation rules, and form generators faster to implement. The underlying calculations and approval rules remain deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear procedures, missing source records, changing form versions, and submissions with legal consequences remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant spots when a formally complete form misrepresents the request and asks the right person to correct it.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving missing information and procedural exceptions. Approval and signing rights do not change.

reach.task: Simplify a recurring internal request procedure.
reach.learn: Process mapping, approval thresholds, and form-version control.

evidence.claim: Structured record fields can populate templates with deterministic validation and approval routing.
Duplicate filing can be removed when the submission system retains the authoritative version and required audit record.

assumptions: The representative scope is routine internal administrative forms, rather than government filings or contract execution.
Forms draw from employee or financial records as appropriate; they do not require both sources in every case.
Request categories and field mappings are explicit, so no model loop is needed.
Only forms requiring authorisation enter the approval step.
The retained submission record can satisfy the applicable retention and audit requirements.
Build ranges cover one form family and two existing source interfaces.
GDPR requires purpose-limited access to personal data. National rules determine any employee consultation needed for changed administrative processes.
unknowns: Form inventory, version ownership, and actual source fields.
Which approvals are mandatory and which are historical habits.
Availability of source interfaces and permitted field-level access.
Whether local copies have a distinct retention requirement.
Whether any forms trigger external commitments or specialised legal requirements.
research_questions: Which forms can disappear because their information already exists in an authoritative record?
Which validation failures need judgment rather than better mandatory fields?
new_work: Maintain field mappings, templates, and procedural rules.
Resolve missing or contradictory source information.
Review required approvals and failed submissions.
Check that retained records remain complete and accessible.

tasks.short: Find the correct supporting files and attach them to correspondence prepared for reply.

steps.what: Read incoming correspondence and identify the request, subject, and relevant record references.

loop.input: Incoming correspondence and permitted reference formats.
loop.output: Requested information, record references, and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate reference formats and identities; display supporting correspondence passages.
loop.stop: One extraction; ambiguous identities or missing references return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reference parsing handles standard identifiers, but requests also describe needs in free text.

steps.what: Search authorised folders and records for candidate supporting files.
Check relevance, version, completeness, and whether files may be shared with the intended recipient.

loop.input: Permission-filtered candidate files, reply requirements, version metadata, and recipient details.
loop.output: Proposed attachment set with relevance passages and unresolved disclosure questions.
loop.check: Apply version and sharing rules deterministically; assistant verifies relevance and recipient entitlement.
loop.stop: Inspect at most ten candidate files once; unresolved relevance or disclosure questions require manual selection.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata checks establish versions and permissions, but cannot always establish relevance to a narrative request.

steps.what: Attach selected files to the reply draft and pass it to the reply owner.

tasks.design: A bounded intake step extracts request details from the {EMAIL}, then an integration searches the {DOCS} using references and permission-filtered metadata. A second bounded step proposes relevant files, while deterministic checks enforce version and sharing rules. The assistant approves the attachment set before the {EMAIL} receives a reply draft for its owner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent file names, missing record references, and fragmented permissions make reliable retrieval difficult. Relevance often depends on reading the request.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration development makes permission-aware search and draft assembly affordable. Small language steps can interpret requests and explain candidate relevance.
tasks.still_hard: Poorly indexed archives, scanned files, duplicate versions, and recipient entitlement remain difficult. Internal read access does not establish permission to disclose externally.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognises when an apparently relevant file exposes unrelated information or answers the wrong question.

ambition.what: Source-linked reply preparation for field coordinators.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching folders toward checking difficult evidence and disclosure questions. The assistant gains no new disclosure authority; a proposed service extends preparation support to field coordinators.

reach.task: Improve document references, version labels, and retrieval metadata.
reach.learn: Records classification, retention schedules, and access-control inheritance.

evidence.claim: Reference-based retrieval, permission filtering, version checks, and draft attachment assembly can use deterministic technology.
Narrative relevance suggestions need source references and human checking before disclosure.

assumptions: Most supporting files are electronic; paper-only archives remain a manual exception.
The document store exposes searchable metadata and enforceable access controls.
The workflow prepares attachments; the reply owner controls sending in the adjoining reply process.
The assistant may approve routine attachment selection under established sharing rules; unclear disclosures go to the information owner.
Build ranges cover one shared mailbox and one document repository.
GDPR applies to search, processing, and disclosure. National rules determine any consultation required for changed working methods.
unknowns: Document-index quality, scanned-file volume, and duplicate-version prevalence.
Whether search interfaces preserve the requesting user's permissions.
Available recipient-entitlement rules and information-owner escalation routes.
Whether attachment versions can be pinned between approval and draft creation.
research_questions: How much retrieval succeeds using record references and metadata alone?
Does relevance assistance reduce total search and checking time?
Can the attachment process detect changed files or recipients after approval?
new_work: Review ambiguous requests and proposed file relevance.
Repair metadata and resolve duplicate versions.
Maintain sharing rules and permission mappings.
Handle changed files, failed attachments, and disclosure escalations.

role.altitude: Routine calendar handling, form entry, document formatting, and file retrieval shrink. The assistant spends more time resolving exceptions, checking evidence, and improving office processes; additional decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Facilities manager: use aggregate booking demand to improve room availability.
Project management specialist: maintain action registers from approved decisions.
Administrative services manager: simplify recurring request procedures.
File clerk: improve document metadata and retrieval quality.
skills_to_grow: Map source fields and validate generated documents.
Apply access, disclosure, and retention rules.
Measure total handling time, including review and exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Run a shared administrative preparation service for office and field staff, with reliable request intake, source-linked documents, and clear escalation routes. Seek delegated authority over routine scheduling and process improvements while document owners retain publication and commitment decisions.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
